records.source_Japanese: おねーちゃん、あそぼー
records.source_meaning: The boy familiarly calls to an older girl/woman and asks her to play; this is not an actual sister relationship.
records.whole_exchange_context: A child named Mao casually asks Maria to play. His mother recognizes her status and panics over her son's supposed disrespect; Maria permits it, then privately feels that only flowers and birds return her affection. In a later private exchange she tells Xien how painful the townspeople's fear is, despite her efforts against the wokou pirates. She recalls her father's death, her vow to become a metaphorical demon and her fearsome source sobriquet 翔緋鯱. Past/present pirate-reputation variants stay separate. Xien invites her to stop pretending with him; she thanks him but resolves to act rather than regret inaction. The child's familiar older-sister address is not kinship, Mao is a contextual personal name rather than a global rename of the shared Boy actor, and no aristocratic title or new violent act is added.

records.speaker: Maria Li
records.context: A child named Mao casually asks Maria to play. His mother recognizes her status and panics over her son's supposed disrespect; Maria permits it, then privately feels that only flowers and birds return her affection. In a later private exchange she tells Xien how painful the townspeople's fear is, despite her efforts against the wokou pirates. She recalls her father's death, her vow to become a metaphorical demon and her fearsome source sobriquet 翔緋鯱. Past/present pirate-reputation variants stay separate. Xien invites her to stop pretending with him; she thanks him but resolves to act rather than regret inaction. The child's familiar older-sister address is not kinship, Mao is a contextual personal name rather than a global rename of the shared Boy actor, and no aristocratic title or new violent act is added.

records.source_meaning: The port worker asks Maria to take this person to a village named Guam; his familiar address does not establish kinship.
records.whole_exchange_context: A European-region port worker asks Maria to take a stranded ceremonial priest to a village called Guam. The language barrier makes the account tentative: a dugout apparently drifted to the Spice Islands, and a Western ship brought him farther from home. He can only point east-northeast. Maria accepts an uncertain travel time. The passenger says xie xie; the worker taught him the Chinese thanks because he expected her to help. No shared fluency, precise location, voyage deadline, fee or invented family relation is added.
